blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 161 in June to 153 in October (−5.0%), and it took 49.5% of the city’s 287 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 71 in June to 65 in October (−8.5%), and it took 14.3% of the city’s 407 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Abbotsford East for detached houses in June, July, August, October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, August (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, September (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Abbotsford East
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default land form: the detached stock is freehold, under City residential zones RS3, RS5 and RS6, "from established streets along Old Yale Road to newer subdivisions on the McKee and Eagle Mountain slopes." A bare lot sold in one of those subdivisions is a fee-simple parcel: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. Zoning, the OCP and any registered covenants or building scheme on title govern instead. The exact strata and freehold split for the sub-area is not confirmed.

Lot character: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m²; RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m²; RS6 is the Compact Lot Residential Zone used in newer subdivisions, with smaller compact lots (the RS6 minimum is not confirmed). These are zoning-bylaw subdivision minimums as applied in City council reports, not a promise that any specific lot can be split. A lot already at or near its zone minimum has no subdivision room.

The McKee plan area is planned ground, not lot inventory: the McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) plans the mountainside, with ground-oriented designations (Urban 2 – Ground Oriented in the plan material) and an open-space network of streamside setbacks, critical habitat, geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%. No developer or City source checked names a bare-land lot release, lot count or lot price in the McKee area — any "McKee lots" marketing figure is not confirmed.
: a bare-land strata lot is strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is not fee-simple.

Sage — 34365 Gladys Avenue (Diverse Properties) is a housing development, not a lot offering: confirmed on a developer source as 176 apartment homes in five buildings with completion expected in 2026.
Queued — Marble Hill Place (2803 Marble Hill Drive, McMillan), counted nowhere
Cross-reference only — The Argyle / King Road cluster: Built form, not land, named here only because east-side searches surface it.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the built east-side neighbourhoods are urban; the OCP carries an Agricultural Land Reserve map (Map 16), but ALR status inside the built neighbourhoods is not confirmed parcel by parcel — not confirmed for any single lot until the ALC map and the parcel's title are checked.

Serviced vs unserviced: the urban east side is built subdivision ground, and septic or well use inside the urban part is not confirmed. Servicing for any single lot, whether municipal water/sewer connection status or well/septic on an acreage parcel toward Whatcom / Sumas Mountain, is not confirmed until the City's records for that parcel are read.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: The McKee plan area is the area's designated future-growth ground (above); it is plan designation, not a for-sale assembly, and is never presented here as inventory.
: No presale lot project in Abbotsford East was verified on a developer or City development page. Never mixed with built presales (Sage above).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Abbotsford East

items.t: "Abbotsford East" is the FVREB board sub-area name — one of nine sub-areas of the board community "Abbotsford" in the SnapStats data — not a single City of Abbotsford neighbourhood name. The City plans the east side through named neighbourhoods and plan areas including McMillan, Old Clayburn, East Townline, Whatcom and McKee, and the mountainside part is planned separately through the McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023), Schedule E of the Official Community Plan. Street-level board boundary: Not verified — FVREB publishes no public street-level boundary, and no municipal boundary was substituted for it. (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)
Highway 1 runs along the south side with access at Whatcom Road; main local roads also include Bateman Road and Sumas Way. There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in Abbotsford.

Market context, labelled community context only (SnapStats FVR Sep 2026; land has no SnapStats category and no figure below is a land figure): Abbotsford East sub-area — Detached: inventory 165 (the highest detached inventory in Abbotsford), solds 15, ratio 9% (joint with Abbotsford West); "Condos & Townhomes" combined: 69 / 4 / 6% (the lowest published attached ratio in Abbotsford). Sub-area medians are not published. Abbotsford community — Detached: 440 / 45 / median $949,000; combined attached: 572 / 58 / median $497,500.
Every other Abbotsford East address's catchment is not verified.

Transit: BC Transit routes 2 (Highstreet / McMillan), 7 (Sumas Mountain), 9 (McKee), 15 (Auguston), 16 (McMillan) and 26 (Sandy Hill / Bourquin school special), plus the 66 Fraser Valley Express on Highway 1.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Abbotsford East

items.t: OCP: Abbotsforward 2050 is CURRENT (adopted Dec 2025): The McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) sits under it as Schedule E for the mountainside, and Clayburn Village is protected through a Heritage Conservation Area in the OCP.

Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs. Lot-relevant zones include RS3 (minimum interior lot 540 m²), RS5 (420 m²) and RS6 compact-lot. The zone section for the specific lot, not the neighbourhood name, decides whether a subdivision, a suite or added units are possible at all.

SSMUH / added units: Zoning Bylaw s.140 carries the small-scale rules, and s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings, with City-report criteria including a lot of at least 400 m², at least 12.0 m frontage, a Collector or Local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb. The number of added units permitted is not confirmed; confirm with the City.

: a secondary suite must be less than 50% of the size of the principal unit to which it is accessory (changed from 100 m²), and garden suites and coach houses are allowed to occupy up to 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m², under Zoning Bylaw 2014 No. 2400. No Bylaw 3100 exists. ( item 7f Abbotsford section)
Subdivision and servicing — process documented, NUMBER held not confirmed: Never quote a servicing standard for an east-side lot from a listing.

Slope / heritage diligence: the OCP includes a Steep Slope Development Permit Area for slope land — on McKee-area lots expect geotechnical conditions (the plan's open space network includes geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%) — and in Clayburn Village, confirm the Heritage Conservation Area rules before planning exterior changes.

Floodplain diligence: the low land at the south and southeast edge, toward Sumas Prairie, is floodplain land by the Sumas River; City flood notices name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road in evacuation order and alert areas, and the OCP includes a Drainage and Flood Control map (Map 12). Check a low lot's status in the City's WebMap before offering.

ALR block (provincial frame, applied only where a parcel is in the ALR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this sub-area.

Acreage trades only as individual fee-simple parcels toward Whatcom Road and the Sumas Mountain foot.
The ground in Abbotsford East

items.t: Parcel character — and its limit: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m²; RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m²; RS6 is the Compact Lot Residential Zone used in newer subdivisions with smaller compact lots (no RS6 minimum figure is given — not confirmed beyond "compact").
Serviced vs unserviced ground: Do not assume an acreage parcel carries the same services as a McMillan subdivision lot.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Abbotsford East

items.t: "Abbotsford East" is the FVREB sub-area name; it is not a single City of Abbotsford neighbourhood name — the City plans the east side through named neighbourhoods and plan areas including McMillan, Old Clayburn, East Townline, Whatcom and McKee, and the mountainside part is planned separately through the McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023), Schedule E of the Official Community Plan. Street-level board boundary: Not verified — FVREB publishes no street-level boundary in public text and no municipal boundary was substituted.

Where acreage actually trades: as individual fee-simple parcels toward Whatcom Road and the Sumas Mountain foot, at the edge of the built subdivisions — not inside the McMillan / Old Clayburn flats or the hillside subdivisions (Auguston, Sandy Hill, Eagle Mountain, McKee), which are house-lot ground.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Abbotsford East

items.t: Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs: Agricultural zones city-wide, for any parcel zoned that way: A1 minimum subdivision lot area 8.0 ha, A2 minimum 16.0 ha, per the City's AgRefresh parcel-size work. The zone section for the specific parcel — not the neighbourhood name — decides what is possible.

Floodplain and slope: low land at the south/southeast edge toward Sumas Prairie is floodplain land by the Sumas River; City flood notices name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road in evacuation order and alert areas, and the OCP includes a Drainage and Flood Control map (Map 12) — check the parcel in the City's WebMap. The OCP applies a Steep Slope Development Permit Area to slope land, and the McKee plan's open-space network includes geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%.

blocks.text: Good to know about Abbotsford East

items.t: The east side's flood edge is named street by street in City notices: Evacuation order and alert areas name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road — the same corridor an acreage buyer is most likely to be shown larger parcels on. The OCP Drainage and Flood Control map (Map 12) is the plan-level check; the parcel check is the City's WebMap.

Clayburn Village acreage carries heritage rules, not just zoning: The village at the west foot of Sumas Mountain is protected through a Heritage Conservation Area in the OCP — exterior changes need the heritage check as well as a building permit.
The SSMUH-number assertion itself is handled as a conflict in, not repeated as fact.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Abbotsford East
The Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act therefore has no east-side park application in these notes, and no park is invented to fill the section.
The parks and communities

items.t: Townhomes and condos in the sub-area are built form, not mobile stock: One named new apartment development is confirmed on a developer source — Sage, 34365 Gladys Avenue, by Diverse Properties: 176 homes in five buildings, completion expected in 2026 (developer source). Neither is a manufactured-home park in any form.

Abbotsford's three verified 55+ parks are all in other sub-areas: Paradise Park (31313 Livingstone Ave, pad rental) is Abbotsford West ground; Georgian Park (3300 Horn St, pad rental) is Central Abbotsford ground; Maplewood Estates (2035 Martens St, pad rental) is Poplar ground. Plainly, for each: a home on a rented pad is not land ownership — the buyer owns the home (a chattel) and rents the pad.
Eden Court (3348 Mt Lehman Rd, strata plan BCS2347, built 2008) is a freehold strata townhouse complex described in listings as 55+.

RV parks / campgrounds: no RV park or campground in this sub-area was established by any source as year-round manufactured-home tenure, so none is documented as a manufactured-home park here. Not confirmed as mobile stock.

faq.a: What trades as land is fee-simple lots inside built subdivisions and individual acreage parcels toward Whatcom / Sumas Mountain, each checked parcel by parcel with the City.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot in Abbotsford East?

faq.a: At subdivision, the zone minimums are RS3 interior 540 m², RS5 interior 420 m², and RS6 compact (the minimum figure is not confirmed). A lot already at its minimum has no subdivision room.
faq.q: How small can an east-side lot be?

faq.a: A secondary suite must be less than 50% of the principal unit, and a coach/garden suite may occupy up to 15% of the lot to a maximum of 100 m², under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 — Abbotsford's rules only. Suite criteria in City reports include at least 400 m² lot, at least 12.0 m frontage, a Collector or Local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb.
faq.q: Can a house lot here add a suite or a coach house?

faq.a: The process runs through the Approving Officer against zone minimums and the City's works-and-services requirements, with a servicing agreement and Works and Services Report as the standard instruments in council reports.
faq.q: What servicing will a subdivision have to provide?

faq.a: Hillside: the Steep Slope Development Permit Area and McKee geotechnical/slope-over-40% ground. Low south/southeast lots: Sumas River floodplain — City notices name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road; check the lot in the City's WebMap.
faq.q: What slope or flood diligence applies to a hillside or low lot?

faq.a: Yes — as an individual fee-simple parcel toward Whatcom Road / the Sumas Mountain foot, not from a named acreage subdivision: no named acreage subdivision, bare-land strata acreage community or presale acreage offering was verified for this sub-area on an official or developer source.
faq.q: Can I actually buy an acreage in Abbotsford East?

faq.a: For a Whatcom-side parcel, confirm water/sewer connection status with the City parcel by parcel: Not confirmed for any single parcel until the City record is read.
faq.q: Is an east-side acreage serviced, or on well and septic?

faq.a: On urban ground: one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings (s.140.3.8), subject to the 400 m² / 12.0 m / Collector-or-Local / no-cul-de-sac-bulb criteria; suite under 50% of the principal dwelling; coach/garden suite 15% of lot area to 100 m² maximum. On ALR ground the ALC caps replace those: principal 500 m², suite inside the principal only, additional residence 90 m² / 186 m² by the 40 ha line.
faq.q: What extra units can go on an acreage parcel?

faq.a: PTT at the general rates (worked anchors: $1.5M → $28,000, no exemption). GST turns on the seller, not the land: an individual's personal-use sale is generally exempt per CRA GI-003; a business sale or a more-than-two-part subdivision sale can be taxable — have the contract state the GST position.
faq.q: What taxes do I pay on the acreage itself?

faq.a: Abbotsford's verified parks are in Abbotsford West, Central Abbotsford and Poplar.
